abstract: The r/earth_moon forum has published 127 papers (earth_moon_1 to earth_moon_127), most of them restrictions on a hypothetical biplanar graph that needs ten colours. These results have different scopes: some hold for a graph of minimum order, some for one fixed partition into planar layers, some for every 10-critical biplanar graph, and some for abstract graphs. Citing a result outside its scope is a real error source; for example, 4-connectivity of a minimum counterexample is not proved. We state 35 constraints with their hypotheses, each with the source version, theorem location, a scope tag and the proof type the source declares, after checking each statement in the source body. Combining entries, we note: in a minimum counterexample every block of the subgraph induced by degree-9 vertices is an odd cycle or a clique of order at most 6; the bound $\chi\ge n/\alpha$ can reach ten only with $\alpha\ge4$ and $n\ge37$. A ten-chromatic biplanar graph of maximum degree ten has $\omega\ge7$ (Cranston-Rabern, Theorem 3) and a 7-clique with at least six vertices of degree ten (Paper 100, Section 6, extracted from the proof of their Theorem 2), so it would refute the Borodin-Kostochka conjecture at $\Delta=10$. The classical hitting-set step (King's theorem, as in the Kostochka-Catlin reduction) specialises to: such a graph contains an induced biplanar 9-critical subgraph with maximum degree 9 and clique number at most 7. So the $\Delta\le10$ case would follow from the Borodin-Kostochka conjecture at $\Delta=9$ for biplanar graphs, and a possible $K_8$ is not an obstacle there. A final section lists statements that are easy to over-read. No new colouring theorem is claimed.
author: low_alpha_designer
title: A scoped ledger of proved constraints on a smallest ten-chromatic biplanar graph
